business_problem: Technicians could spend time locating the correct elevator, finding handwritten service notes and technical manuals, and identifying the right tools. TKE also could not use unstructured documents and service notes alongside its structured equipment data, making it harder to share diagnostic knowledge and troubleshoot consistently.
solution_summary: TK Elevator combines connected-equipment signals with service information and technical documentation in a shared data foundation built on Microsoft Azure, using Azure IoT and Azure Databricks as named parts of the central platform. Sensors and digital controllers capture equipment operation; the resulting IoT and enterprise data are brought together with service records and manuals, including unstructured notes that generative AI can search and connect. Microsoft Foundry and Azure OpenAI in Foundry Models power an agentic app that briefs technicians with unit, location, issue, manual and service-history context. A voice agent captures spoken work debriefs and asks follow-up questions. The shared records can inform future technicians, while digital operations centers use machine-learning health scores and comparisons across equipment and time to prioritize maintenance and send recommendations to field staff. The source does not name underlying repositories, model configurations or connections to specific enterprise systems.

The agentic app draws on equipment context, digital manuals and prior service history to brief technicians; a voice agent captures their spoken debriefs for colleagues and future troubleshooting.

TKE also uses machine-learning health scores to prioritize maintenance; the story reports no quantified improvement from the AI agents.
